text:
No, we can't certify that. What the evidence supports is narrower: NASA FIRMS recorded no thermal detections intersecting ASSET-F06 between 2026-10-06 and 2026-11-05. All four sensors (VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21 and MODIS) covered every day of that period, so the absence of detections isn't a coverage gap.

However, the tool explicitly states this does not establish that no fire occurred. Small, short-lived, cool or cloud-obscured fires can go undetected. The result also says nothing about burned area, the cause of any change on the land, or anything outside this period.

A safe wording would be: "No FIRMS thermal anomalies were detected within the asset boundary during the period, with full sensor coverage." If you need stronger assurance, you would need complementary evidence such as burned-area mapping, optical imagery review, or ground confirmation.

Note the data used near-real-time products and the knowledge date is 2026-11-12.
